text:
anna: Quick context — dashboard queries for large tenants are showing a 3x fanout in the query layer when RBAC checks hit the projection services. Traced it to per-tenant permission expansion on the tile renderer. Thinking we should try a small "lease-bridge" approach: a single lightweight authz/lease fetch that other components can reuse for the request window.

mike: +1 on reducing duplicate checks. tradeoff is a serialized dependency and possible cold-path latency. How do you keep it from becoming a hot-spot? :thinking:

anna: agree about hot-spot. plan is: short TTL per request (50-200ms), async refresh for longer work, and sticky routing to avoid cross-machine churn. also use local cache with fast invalidation keyed by request id/tenant.

sam: can we sketch the interface? do we want the bridge to return a pre-authorized token or just a permission set?

jess: prefer a permission set + version id. tokens add signing complexity and lifespan issues. permission set lets downstream decide what to cache. e.g.,
```
GET /lease-bridge?tenant_id=123&req_id=xyz -> { perms: ["dash:read","panel:exec"], v: "v12" }
```
Downstreams check v and decide cache policy.

ria: operational concerns: telemetry + circuit breaker. If the bridge fails we need graceful degradation to per-service local checks (so we don't block dashboards). Also rate-limit per-tenant.

mike: +1 on graceful fallback. For SLOs we should set a hard 30ms budget for the bridge in the critical path; anything slower uses fallback. We should add sampling traces to measure end-to-end added latency.

anna: noted. another tradeoff — RBAC semantics: must ensure the bridge is authoritative for a rollout, otherwise you'll get inconsistent views across services during cutover. Need a rollout plan:
- leader promotion step to enable bridge authoritative for a subset of tenants
- shadow mode where services call bridge but still perform local checks and compare results
- metrics: mismatch rate, added latency, error-rate on bridge

sam: shadow mode is a must. Also suggest a flag per-route so dashboards can opt into fast-path once they pass divergence thresholds.

jess: implementation thought: put bridge in front of our existing query multiplexer as a sidecar; sidecar can co-locate with the tile renderer to keep rtt low. Sidecar registers local leases and updates central store async.

ria: add ops-bot note — please create a dashboard for: bridge latency P50/P95, mismatch rate (shadow vs local), tenant QPS, circuit tripped count. Also alert if mismatch_rate > 0.1% for 30m.

ops-bot: created issue INF-9876 and dashboard link https://redwood.internal/d/INF-9876/lease-bridge-health :white_check_mark:

mike: perf experiment idea: add a lightweight prefetch in the console proxy for the top 3 tenants per user session. That reduces cold path load without touching the query layer. Might be lower-risk initial win.

anna: good low-risk step. Plan: 1) proxy prefetch experiment (A/B), 2) build lease-bridge in shadow, 3) promote for small tenant cohort, 4) full cutover with gradual ramp and strict SLO rollback. I'll draft a follow-up RFC with interface sketches and rollout checklist.

sam: would love to see perf numbers for step 1 before we invest in the bridge. Who owns the experiment?

jess: I'll own the proxy prefetch experiment. will post results next week.

anna: thanks — tagging @mike and @ria for SLO/alerts review while jess runs the experiment. :thumbsup:
